note: Animal models demonstrate perinatal-lethal cleft palate and severe facial hypoplasia from neural crest BRD4 loss, providing strong mechanistic footing for assessing whether fetal human presentations disproportionately manifest structural clefting compared to postnatal cohorts.

evidence.text: Neural crest cell-specific mutation of Brd4 in mice results in perinatal lethality accompanied by severe facial hypoplasia, cleft palate, and mid-facial clefting due to impaired RUNX2 osteoblast differentiation program regulation.

source.title: BRD4 binds to active cranial neural crest enhancers to regulate RUNX2 activity during osteoblast differentiation
source.quote: Mice with BRD4 NCC loss of function died at birth with severe facial hypoplasia, cleft palate, mid-facial clefting and exencephaly.

evidence.text: An international cohort study of BRD4-related syndrome compiled 14 individuals, including prenatal fetopathological examinations alongside pediatric and adult presentations, establishing age-dependent phenotypic delineation.

source.title: Understanding the new BRD4‐related syndrome: Clinical and genomic delineation with an international cohort study
source.quote: We formed an international collaborative study, and collected 14 new patients, including two fetuses. We performed phenotype and genotype analysis, integrated prenatal findings from fetopathological examinations, phenotypes of pediatric patients and adults.
